We read something about Islamic law in yak collective a while back and since then I've been thinking that there is probably a best seller in writing about how the US and Iran are similar. Also Gramsci Theme parks https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cmy0r96xygx6o

https://summerlightning.substack.com/p/gramsci-theme-parks

Fareed Zakaria wrote a book in 2003 called The Future of Freedom: Illiberal democracy at home and abroad anticipating where we are now, and arguing that democracy leads to illiberalism. Iran is the norm, pre-Trump US the exception, and we’ve regressed to the mean. I recall Zakaria specifically calling out Iran on CNN as an example of illiberal democracy and warning that westerners think liberal and democracy go together like PB&J. They don’t. They’re in deep tension. Arguably modern constitutional states are entirely about managing that tension. It’s the old tyranny of democracy problem. Historically, liberalism has always been a minority bourgeois ethos in opposition to tyranny of both top and bottom.

Everyone in the middle is either attempting to escape upward by latching onto the AI boom or by LARPing Dickensian social norms or being forced downward, which means there likely won't be a visible middle class much longer. There will be an invisible bottom class and all the middle classes will be bunched together like three proletariats in a trench coat pretending to be Victorian or something.

Case in point is the numerous recent articles and takes I've seen that are take downs of TV, which arguably is the invention that has defined the middle class more than any other technology after the car . https://www.slowboring.com/p/there-arent-100-good-tv-shows
